sm: The host describes a Friday night nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA that stranded or disrupted about 1.5 million Americans, at the same time Microsoft services went down. He plays the press conference where the DHS Secretary blamed patches and new equipment overwhelming the older system, while the Transportation Secretary tried to stop him by bumping his arm. The host mocks the exchange, says the wording personally implicated Duffy, and notes it came after the midterms. He also questions the claim that a veteran doing the router install rules out sabotage, arguing that systemic incompetence is the likelier and harder problem to fix.

The host then turns to Duffy's demand for more money. He points out that Republicans control Congress and could pass funding through budget reconciliation again, and he cites a government report finding most FAA systems unsustainable and Duffy's point that the routers date from 2001. He asks why a risky router install was done at a peak travel time, notes that Duffy said nobody will be fired, and compares that to a pizza place job. He describes the FAA's account of the El Dorado, Arkansas router and compares it to a 2009 outage caused by a Harris technician, concluding that money does not fix incompetence.

The host draws an analogy between NASA and SpaceX, arguing that NASA gets about 24 billion dollars a year yet has been outclassed by a company that is private and far less funded. He blames declining competence in institutions and argues that government agencies should be defunded while companies like SpaceX are empowered. He then describes SpaceX catching the Starship upper stage after it orbited the Earth, the first time the ship itself was caught, and plays the footage. He says it should inspire pride and calls it a rare moment for optimism.

He criticizes online reactions that ask why the money is not spent on housing and healthcare, and he disputes the claim that the space shuttle already did this, saying reuse could cut launch costs by around 99 percent. He argues that wealth is not zero sum, citing the Memphis mayor saying data centers brought 54 million dollars in taxes, and he praises orbital data centers and Starlink. He answers the healthcare complaints with several points, including that space technology led to medical devices and that progress should not wait for perfect healthcare. He ends the stretch by harshly insulting the commenters.

The host continues attacking commenters who claim they do not care about the SpaceX achievement, saying they cannot feel awe and that the mission is a step toward moon bases and Mars. He responds to a post saying SpaceX simply applied capital and engineering, noting that Blue Origin had far more private funding yet just destroyed its launch pad in a test, and that Boeing and Lockheed received more government money without matching results. He says that success is hard no matter the funding and that mocking failure is the habit of useless people. He argues the country should back extraordinary builders over federal bureaucrats, plays more footage of the catch, and closes by saying the optimistic vision of the future beats the alternative after a week of outages.
